transcription: Main article text only (site header and menus, the hero banner image and its bare 'Credit: NIST' caption, the in-page anchor nav ('SI Model | Defining Constants | Base and Derived Units | Prefixes | Writing with the SI'), 'Return to Top of Page' utility links, the tags block, the contacts block, the 'EXPLORE THE METRIC PROGRAM' footer nav and the 'Created April 12, 2010, Updated July 22, 2025' line removed). Descriptive image captions kept as printed lines with their 'Credit:' lines ('A graphical model of the International System of Units (SI), adapted from NIST Technical Note 938.', 'NIST SP 1247', 'Table of SI base units.'); the images themselves are not stored. The 'Useful Definitions' accordion is kept as its summary heading plus • bullet definitions; inside it the Adobe Stock photo of the Washington Monument and its caption/credit are removed (third-party image), and the 'Resources for Students and Teachers' promo accordion (a list of resource links including third-party items) is removed. Superscripts rendered with ^ (m^2, m^3, 10^30, 10^−30); subscripts flattened (hW). The page's own soft hyphens inside justified text ('mathe­matical', 'sym­bols', 'magni­tude', 'profession­als') are kept as served. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: structure of the International System of Units — the seven defining constants, the seven base units (meter, second, mole, ampere, kelvin, candela, kilogram), the 22 derived units with special names (the twenty-nine-unit core set), the twenty-four prefixes ranging from 10^30 to 10^−30, the 1875 Treaty of the Meter and its bodies (CGPM, CIPM, BIPM), and quantity/unit/value definitions with the worked Washington Monument example (hW = 169 m, numerical value 169). Fits a compare table of the base units, quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the counts and the worked example, and a concept map of the SI structure.
